facts.statement: Yinlong is a basal ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of China.
facts.quote: Yinlong (, meaning "hidden dragon") is a genus of basal ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Period of China.

facts.statement: Yinlong is the earliest known ceratopsian and was a small, primarily bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: By far the earliest known ceratopsian, it was a small, primarily bipedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Yinlong was described and named in 2006 by a team of American and Chinese paleontologists including Xu Xing and Catherine Forster.
facts.quote: A coalition of American and Chinese paleontologists, including Xu Xing, Catherine Forster, Jim Clark, and Mo Jinyou, described and named Yinlong in 2006.

facts.statement: The genus name Yinlong means "hidden dragon" and references the movie Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Mandarin Chinese words 隱 (yǐn: "hidden") and 龍 (lóng: "dragon"), a reference to the movie Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon

facts.statement: The species name downsi honors William Randall Downs III, who died the year before the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The species was named after the American vertebrate paleontologist William Randall Downs III, a frequent participant in paleontological expeditions to China who died the year before Yinlong was discovered.

facts.statement: The first fossil was an exceptionally well-preserved skeleton found in 2004 in the Shishugou Formation of Xinjiang Province, China.
facts.quote: The first specimen discovered was a single exceptionally well-preserved skeleton, complete with skull, of a nearly adult animal, found in 2004 in the Middle-Late Jurassic strata of the Shishugou Formation located in Xinjiang Province, China.

facts.statement: Yinlong lived during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 161.2 to 155.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Yinlong was discovered in an upper section of this formation which dates to the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, or 161.2 to 155.7 million years ago.

facts.statement: Yinlong was a small dinosaur reaching 1.2 meters in length and 10 kilograms in body mass.
facts.quote: Yinlong was a relatively small dinosaur, reaching 1.2 m in length and 10 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: Yinlong is a ceratopsian despite having a skull that lacks a frill and horns.
facts.quote: Despite a virtually frill-less and totally hornless skull, Yinlong is a ceratopsian.

facts.statement: Yinlong had long robust hindlimbs and shorter three-fingered forelimbs, suggesting a bipedal lifestyle.
facts.quote: Long robust hindlimbs and shorter slender forelimbs with three-fingered hands suggests a bipedal lifestyle like many small ornithopods.

facts.statement: A small rostral bone on the upper jaw identifies Yinlong as a ceratopsian.
facts.quote: A small rostral bone on the end of the upper jaw clearly identifies Yinlong as a ceratopsian

facts.statement: Features on Yinlong's skull roof are considered unique shared traits of the group Marginocephalia, which includes both pachycephalosaurs and ceratopsians.
facts.quote: The presence of these features in Yinlong indicates these as actual synapomorphies (unique features) of the larger group Marginocephalia, which contains both the pachycephalosaurs and the ceratopsians

facts.statement: Skull features in Yinlong resemble those of Heterodontosauridae, supporting the hypothesis that these groups are closely related.
facts.quote: Yinlong also preserves skull features reminiscent of the family Heterodontosauridae, providing support for the hypothesis that heterodontosaurids are closely related to marginocephalians

facts.statement: Yinlong is classified within the family Chaoyangsauridae.
Seven gastroliths were preserved in the abdominal cavity of a Yinlong specimen.
facts.quote: Yinlong was discovered with seven gastroliths preserved in the abdominal cavity.

facts.statement: A hypothesis linking Heterodontosauridae and Marginocephalia was not supported by subsequent analyses of Yinlong's postcranial anatomy.
facts.quote: However, this hypothesis was not supported by a subsequent analysis of basal ornithischians that was carried out as part of a study on the postcranial anatomy of Yinlong, which resolved the below phylogeny of Ceratopsia.

rejected.statement: A 2024 study suggested that Yinlong reached sexual maturity at 6 years old.
rejected.quote: In 2024, bone histology based on specimens of various ontogenetic stage (1 early juvenile, 2 late juveniles, 4 subadults and 3 adults) suggested that Yinlong reached sexual maturity at 6 years old
